lead: A 1920s colony turned into a hillside neighbourhood, in the upper part of the city.
text: It took shape between 1915 and 1930 as the Colonia Taxonera, founded by Joaquim Taxonera Cassà, a footwear manufacturer who owned the old Can Grau estate and divided it into plots following a 1902 project. During the 20th century it received a great deal of immigration from the rest of Spain and lacked basic services until the 1980s and 1990s. La Bòbila, a brickworks from 1906 that operated for more than a hundred years, is being turned into a community and cultural centre, with an investment of 6.3 million euros, and the Pla de Barris 2025-2028 includes the neighbourhood among the mountain neighbourhoods, with work on public space and accessibility.

Today it is a compact neighbourhood, with 12,727 inhabitants in 0.34 km² and 37,654 inhabitants/km², and the El Coll | La Teixonera station on line 5 gives it a direct link to the centre. At 2,951 €/m², its prices are among the most affordable in Horta-Guinardó. If you are selling, the average sale price is 14% below the Horta-Guinardó average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 236,000 € on average, and this neighbourhood sits in the middle band of Horta-Guinardó (9th of 11 by price). If you are investing, the average rent (865 €/month) is 5% below the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: Blocks and houses on the hillside, on steeply sloping streets.
places: Estació de metro El Coll | La Teixonera
